versions.short: The bill would change a US customs law so that Customs and Border Protection could share certain nonpublic information about suspected counterfeit or infringing goods with the people who hold intellectual property rights in them, and would extend that sharing to goods whose packaging, packing materials, containers, and labels appear to infringe. It would let the agency provide such information when it has a reasonable suspicion of a violation, rather than only when it suspects one, and would allow sharing of information generated by online marketplaces, express consignment operators, freight forwarders, and other businesses involved in bringing goods into the United States. When such information is shared, the agency would have to notify the affected party of what was transmitted, following rules set by the Secretary. The bill would also widen the list of parties who could receive this information to include any other party with an interest in the goods, as the Commissioner determines appropriate.
